$comment: D4.49 — Normalisation idempotence. What was required, what was done, the evidence, and what remains open.
Measured on 21 October 2026 against the D4.48 tree (the D4.48 patch applied to GitHub 223bfc821) and the D4.49 working tree. Engineering only: no legal content changed.

items.requirement: Normalisation is a fixed point: a second pass over a finished document changes nothing, and no document ships a capitalised role word it does not define.
found: Measured: on the D4.48 engine, a second normalizeClauseText over the 58 fixture documents (29 types x WELL_FILLED, MINIMAL_DECLINED) changed 8 clauses in 6 documents: NDA_DISCLOSURE_PERMITTED_001 ('the Recipient'), LOAN_AMOUNT_001 ('a Principal sum' to 'a Borrower sum'), IP_LICENSE_001 and IP_LICENSE_RESTRICTIONS_001 ('the Licensor'/'the Licensee'). Over the clause library, 8 of 8,146 normalisations were not idempotent, among them 'as if the Intern were an Intern' and 'a Distributor-seller basis'.

Traced stage by stage, the D4.47 diagnosis (text inserted by the quality controls after normalisation) was wrong. Each word was created by the first normalisation pass: the hardening renderers write lower-case 'the recipient', 'the licensor', 'a principal sum'; replaceRoleAliases is case-sensitive and left them; normalizeRoleCapitalization then capitalised aliases as well as canonical roles. The normaliser manufactured the aliases it exists to remove.
done: backend/services/clauseQualityNormalizer.js: normalizeRoleCapitalization capitalises only the canonical role ('the receiving party' to 'the Receiving Party'). An alias is only ever replaced; a lower-case alias is ordinary English and is left as written.
No extra normalisation stage and no new masking were needed, so none was added: once the rule stopped manufacturing aliases, the existing single pass is a fixed point.
documentService.js: the survival stage's comment updated; it still normalises only the clauses it re-renders, because the quality controls are not proven idempotent.
items.result: 0 of 8,154 library normalisations and 0 clauses of the 58 fixture documents change on a second pass. Shipped text changed in 21 conservation cases, each a correction: the NDA's 'the recipient' (and 'the recipient Party' in its notices clause, as every other agreement already read), the loan's 'a principal sum', the Software Development Agreement's lower-case 'licensor'/'licensee', and the Distribution Agreement's 'a buyer-seller basis' (it had shipped 'a Distributor-seller basis'). Nothing else moved: no finding, score, certification or clause order.
items.verified_by: tests/normalisationIdempotence.test.mjs (37 checks: frozen defect, regression, positive, negative, boundary, library-wide and corpus-wide idempotence)

records_updated: document-quality-standard.json: NORMALISATION_NOT_IDEMPOTENT FIXED_D4_49, with the corrected diagnosis; its next_sequence item DONE_D4_49.
mutation-paths.json: the D4.47 exception notes the fix.
still_open: The NDA and the Software Development Agreement now say 'the recipient' and 'the licensor'/'the licensee' in lower case: ordinary words, no longer undefined defined terms. Whether those clauses should name the defined roles instead ('the Receiving Party') is a drafting choice for the advocate; in a licence clause the direction of the licence can run either way, which is why the generic words were kept.
The quality controls (documentQualityControl.js) are not proven idempotent; the survival stage still avoids re-running them over the whole document.

accepted.decision: Accepted as engineering-complete on the evidence reported, pending integration into GitHub main (D4.48 then D4.49, in the verified order 223bfc821 -> e7c0ad689c -> 76d352a91b).
qualifications: Idempotence is not semantic correctness. The tests prove that a second pass changes nothing over the tested corpus; they do not prove that every normalised clause is substantively correct. A normaliser can repeat a wrong result exactly.

The terminology question is decided per document, not by a universal rule. Whether 'recipient', 'licensor' and 'licensee' should be defined terms in the NDA and the Software Development Agreement depends on each instrument's parties, definitions and obligations; the document's approved terminology decides whether a role word is a defined term or an ordinary noun. No universal capitalisation rule is to be introduced.
Normaliser idempotence is established; idempotence of the whole generation and quality-control sequence is not. The two stay separate in this record until the latter is measured.
